title: The regular coefficient module is the scalar telescope
statement: For each scheme X the sequence of regular integral coefficient modules under multiplication by ℓ has a colimit cocone whose vertex is isomorphic to the restricted regular continuous E coefficient module. The zeroth leg, under this isomorphism, is the actual coefficient inclusion. Definitions and notation: [def-weil-pbc-integral-localization-telescope].

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), referring to Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.2; scalar localization telescope

proof.text: Reuse the presheaf scalar telescope, its colimit proof, and the monoidal coefficient isomorphisms from ContinuousIntegralScalarExact through a proof-only import all. Sheafification and inverse image from the point preserve that colimit. Transport it along the regular coefficient isomorphisms using transportRegularTelescope; naturality of the coefficient comparison identifies its zeroth leg with the actual coefficient inclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem integralRegularTelescope (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃ c : Cocone (integralLocalizationSequence ℓ (Mod.regular
        (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X))),
      Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧
      ∃ e : c.pt ≅ (Mod.comap (D := Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
          (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) X)).obj
          (Mod.regular (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X)),
        (c.ι.app 0 ≫ e.hom).hom = coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) X
